steps.name: Removing the bag
dialogues: Let's start with the first step: bag removal.
First, let's go over all the materials you'll need: your new bag, cleaning wipes or adhesive remover, and a disposal bag.
To remove your current bag, stretch your skin with one hand and gently peel the plaque from top to bottom.
This helps reduce discomfort and protects your skin from overstretching.
Many people wonder what the best way to remove the adhesive plaque from their skin is.
Let's see if you can answer this question...
Using a spray remover or an adhesive wipe is much gentler on the skin.
These products dissolve the adhesive, making it easier to remove without causing trauma to the skin.
Pulling directly can damage the skin and cause pain or irritation.
It's a small measure that can make a big difference in your daily comfort.
Let's practice!
Grab the spray and drag it to the stoma bag attached to the body.
Next, remove the stoma bag and put in the waste bag.
steps.question: What is best to use to make plaque removal easier?
answers: A spray remover or an adhesive wipe
Pulling the plaque directly with your hands

steps.name: Cleaning the stoma
dialogues: Now that we have removed the bag, it is time to clean the stoma and the skin around it.
The stoma is bright red and may bleed a little while you clean it, don't worry, this is normal.
Cleaning is a crucial step to prevent skin irritation.
Remember that the stoma does not have any nerve endings, so you will not feel pain when touching it, but it is still important to be gentle.
Let's see if you know what is the best method for cleaning...
Warm water or saline is all you need.
Soaps, especially scented or antibacterial soaps, can leave residue on the skin that interferes with the adhesion of the plate and can cause irritation.
A practical tip: use soft gauze or non-abrasive tissues for cleaning.
Pat gently instead of scrubbing, and be sure to dry the skin thoroughly before applying the new plate.
Dry skin ensures better adhesion of the system.
Let's practice!
Grab the water and drag it to the cloth to wet it.
Grab the wet cloth and drag it to the stoma area.
steps.question: What is best to clean the skin around the stoma?

steps.name: Measuring your stoma
dialogues: Measuring your stoma is a crucial step that is often overlooked.
Your stoma can change in size over time, especially in the first few weeks after surgery, so it is important to measure it regularly.
To measure your stoma, use a measuring guide, often provided in stoma kits.
Place the guide over your stoma and find the hole that best matches your stoma size.
Let's talk about how big the hole in the adhesive baseplate should be...
If your stoma measures 28 mm, the hole in the baseplate should be 29–30 mm, leaving only a small margin of 1–2 mm around the stoma.
It is a common misconception that a smaller hole will prevent leakage, but in reality it can damage the stoma, causing ulcers or circulatory problems.
On the other hand, a hole that is too large will leave too much skin exposed to secretions, causing irritation.
If you have difficulty measuring your stoma yourself, do not hesitate to ask a family member for help or contact your stoma care nurse.
Let's practice!
Grab the measurement board and drag it to the stoma.
As you can see, the best measurement is 30 mm.
Now, drag the scissors to the new stoma bag to cut it.
steps.question: Your stoma measures 28 mm. How big do you cut the hole in the adhesive?
answers: 29–30 mm, to leave a minimal margin
25 mm, so it grips better and prevents leakage

steps.name: Skin protection
dialogues: Protection of the peristomal skin is essential to prevent irritation and ensure good adhesion of the system.
If the area around the stoma has irregularities, such as scars, folds or depressions, leaks may occur that cause skin irritation.
Let's see what to do in these cases...
Modeling paste or barrier ring are invaluable tools for creating a uniform surface.
These products fill in irregularities in the skin, creating a smooth base for the plate to adhere to and preventing leaks.
Modeling paste is applied directly to folds or depressions and should be left to dry for a few minutes before applying the plate.
The barrier ring, on the other hand, can be modeled with your fingers to perfectly fit the shape of your stoma.
A tip: if you use modeling paste, slightly moisten your fingers with water to prevent the paste from sticking to your hands during application.
Let's practice!
Grab the barrier ring and drag it to the stoma area.
steps.question: You have an irregular peristomal area. What do you use?

steps.name: Applying the plate
dialogues: Now we are ready to apply the new plate.
This step requires precision and patience, but you will see that with practice it will become easier and easier.
Remove the protective film from the adhesive plate.
Center the plate hole around the stoma and apply the plate to the skin, starting from the bottom up to avoid the formation of folds.
There is a little trick to ensure good adhesion. Let's see if you know it...
Maintaining pressure on the plate for at least 1-2 minutes is essential to activate the adhesive and ensure an optimal seal.
The warmth of your hand helps the adhesive to blend better with the skin.
An extra tip: gently massage from the inside out of the plate, following a circular motion.
This helps eliminate any air bubbles and further improves adhesion.
Don't be afraid to press firmly, the system is designed to withstand this pressure.
Let's practice!
Grab the cut stoma bag and drag it to the stoma area.
steps.question: How long should you hold the plate down for good adhesion?
answers: No time, it sticks on its own
